evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-01"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-01". POST with no dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The value is a plain YYYY-MM-DD date with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/2 with {"dueDate":"2026-11-11"} returned 200 and the new date. PATCH with {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null. PATCH with {"dueDate":"2026-01-05"} returned 200 and set that date.
evidence.AC3: These requests all returned HTTP 400 with the error 'dueDate must be YYYY-MM-DD or null': POST with "2026-02-30", POST with "23.10.2026", POST with "2026-10-23T10:00:00Z", and PATCH with "2026-02-30".
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-10-23. I created these todos: past (due 2026-10-01), future (2026-12-01, later changed to 2026-01-05), today (due 2026-10-23), nodue (no date) and pastdone (due 2026-09-01, marked done). GET /todos?overdue=true returned only 'past' and 'future' (the latter after its date was moved to 2026-01-05). The todo due today, the one without a date and the done one were all excluded.
evidence.AC5: The page at / lists each todo with its due date: 'past · fällig 01.10.2026', 'future · fällig 05.01.2026', 'today · fällig 23.10.2026' and 'pastdone ✓ · fällig 01.09.2026'. 'nodue' shows no date.
evidence.AC6: On the list page, 'past' and 'future' (now due 05.01.2026) carry the word 'überfällig'. The todo due today, the one without a date and the done todo with a past date do not.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. After I clicked it, the list showed only 'past' and 'future'.
